claims.text: Direct aging promotes formation of L1₂ precipitates in multiprincipal-element alloys.
Direct aging promotes formation of L2₁ precipitates in multiprincipal-element alloys.
Formation of L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates enhances oxidation resistance during sustained high-temperature exposure.
Formation of L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates preserves material integrity during sustained high-temperature exposure.
L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates stabilize the alloy microstructure.
L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates impede grain-boundary diffusion.
L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates provide nucleation sites for oxide formation.
Precipitate-assisted oxide nucleation promotes formation of a coherent and protective oxide layer.
Reduced diffusion of reactive species such as oxygen delays disruptive oxidation.
Mitigation of microstructural coarsening helps maintain mechanical integrity at high temperature.
Direct-aged samples will develop thinner oxide scales than unaged samples under identical oxidation conditions.
Direct-aged samples will develop more uniform oxide scales than unaged samples.
Direct-aged samples will develop more adherent oxide scales than unaged samples.
Direct-aged samples will exhibit less grain coarsening than unaged samples after oxidation exposure.
Direct-aged samples will retain more of their mechanical properties than unaged samples after oxidation exposure.
Untreated samples are expected to form less controlled oxide scales under the same high-temperature oxidation conditions.
Untreated samples are expected to deteriorate faster than direct-aged samples under the same high-temperature oxidation conditions.
The proposed beneficial behavior is expected to hold approximately from 900°C to 1100°C.
Diffusion and precipitate phase stability govern behavior within the proposed temperature and duration range.
Different oxidation mechanisms may dominate at very low or extremely high temperatures outside the proposed range.
